title: The pickaxe
brief:
An API key (`hunter2`) briefly lived in this repo. Security wants the full story: when did it appear, and when did it leave. `git log` alone will not tell you: you need the commits where the string's footprint actually changed.

`git log -S hunter2 --oneline` (the "pickaxe") lists exactly those commits: the one that added the key and the one that scrubbed it.

Run the pickaxe, then check out the scrub commit to verify what it did. Detached HEAD is fine: you are inspecting, not building.

goals.label: You are at the scrub commit

hints: git log -S hunter2 --oneline. Two commits come up: the leak and the scrub.
git checkout <sha> of the LATER one (the scrub).
The pickaxe counts occurrences per commit and reports where the count changed. It answers 'when did this text change', which message-search cannot.
